conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I’ll be taking care of you tonight. Can you tell me what’s been going on?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Hi… I’ve been having this terrible pain in my stomach again. Right in the middle. It came on suddenly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. Was it different from your usual pain?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, it’s the same—really sharp, makes me nauseous, and I threw up a couple times. No blood though.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Any fever or chills?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, no fever. But I was sweating a lot when it started.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. I see you were seen by your gastroenterologist earlier today and sent here. We’ve reviewed your records. You’ve had this kind of pain before, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, many times. They’ve done so many tests—ultrasounds, scopes, CTs. Nothing ever shows up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s tough. We’re going to check your vitals and labs to make sure nothing’s changed. Your blood sugar was high when you arrived—347. Are you on insulin?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, glargine at night and Humalog with meals. But I haven’t eaten much because of the pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s important. Taking mealtime insulin without eating can drop your sugar too low. We’ll monitor that closely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your white blood cell count is high—22.2. That’s been a pattern for you, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it’s always high. Doctors say it’s from stress or my body reacting to pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s possible. We also see microcytic anemia—low hemoglobin and small red cells. That could be from iron deficiency, which you’ve had before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I take iron pills, but I forget sometimes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll keep you on those. Now, because your IV access has been difficult in the past, we placed a line in your groin for fluids and meds. It’s temporary.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I know… I’ve had ports before, but they got infected. I don’t want another one.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Understood. This line will come out before you go home. We’re giving you fluids, anti-nausea meds, and your usual tramadol for pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: How are you feeling now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: A little better. The pain’s not as sharp. But I feel groggy.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You got several doses of lorazepam in the ER for anxiety and pain. That can make you drowsy. We’ll go easy on sedatives now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I just want the pain to stop. It’s so frustrating when no one can find the cause.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I hear you. Based on your history and all the tests you’ve had, this seems like a flare of your chronic pain, possibly linked to your anxiety. We’re not seeing signs of infection or a surgical issue.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. I reviewed your urine test from last night.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is it another UTI? I get those a lot.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The culture grew Klebsiella pneumoniae, a bacteria that’s resistant to several antibiotics. But you don’t have fever, burning, or urgency—so it’s likely not an active infection. We won’t treat it now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: But could it be causing the pain?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Unlikely. Your pain is in the upper belly, not the pelvis. And your white count has been chronically high without infection. We’re watching blood cultures, but so far, no growth.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your pain seems much better. You’re moving more easily and not crying out. How do you feel?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, it’s way better. The tramadol and Zofran are helping. I even sipped some broth.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Great. We’re going to remove the femoral line later today. It’s a risk for infection, especially with your history.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Please do. I don’t want another infection like last time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I need to talk about something important. Last night, your blood sugar dropped—you were shaky and confused.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I didn’t eat dinner… but I took my Humalog anyway. I didn’t think.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s exactly what happened. We gave you juice and glucagon, and you recovered. But it’s dangerous. If you skip a meal, skip the Humalog. Your long-acting insulin stays, but not the meal dose.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll remember. I just get so mixed up when I’m in pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll go over your insulin again before you leave. Your sugars are stable now—136 this morning.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing well. Pain’s gone, you’re eating, and labs are improving. We’d like to send you home today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s good. What about the bacteria in my urine?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Still no signs of infection, so no antibiotics. But your daughter should follow up on the blood cultures—we’ll call if they grow anything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my pain? What do I do when it comes back?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Use your tramadol as prescribed, stay hydrated, and try relaxation techniques. If vomiting or fever starts, come back. Otherwise, call your PCP.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my insulin—I won’t forget again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good. We’re sending all your meds home. Your daughter will get discharge instructions too.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just a final check. You’re alert, pain-free, and walking. We’re clearing you to go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I’m glad this episode is over.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care. Call if anything changes. We’re here if you need us.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thanks for listening.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Of course. That’s what we’re here for.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel better knowing you checked everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We did. And you’re safe to go. Rest well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take it easy.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll try.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s all we can ask.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: See you next time, hopefully not soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hopefully not. But we’ll be ready if you are.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s comforting.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care. We’ll see you in follow-up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Doctor.
